note: What a fence thinks one item is worth, in credits (D-125). The worth is the cheapest honest price of the item where one exists (the cities' shelves and the regional exchange), so a fence, who pays at most 60 percent of it, never pays more than the item costs to buy. Items with no worth here are not bought at all: nothing a person can come by for free (stone, logs, dirt) and nothing worthless (paper, bread).
